<reason>Both sides argued competently and stayed on the motion, but A did more damaging comparative work. A's core claim — that financial liability converts the institution into a defendant whose lawyers' first duty is to withhold registers and burial records — was concrete, grounded in plausible real cases (Canada's "best efforts" collapse, Ireland's indemnity) without brittle precision, and it survived. B's best repair was "no archives, no discharge," but A turned that into the debate's cleanest kill: discharge is finality, so B had reinvented the Irish indemnity with a better preface, and no body can certify the completeness of an archive whose index the defendant supplied. B's closing asserted the church "does not buy immunity with curated files" but never supplied a mechanism to answer the completeness problem. A also extracted a real concession under pressure — B conceded the fund pays from state seed money — and used it to argue the survivor's cheque is identical under both models, so the only thing purchased by contribution is release. B's counter-flip ("then the only question is who ultimately carries the cost," which is the motion's own question) was the best moment of B's case and kept B live, and B landed a good hit with "land is money — you concede the principle while fighting the label," which A only partially distinguished. But B dropped that line in later rounds instead of pressing it, and B's reply to A's leverage answer (subpoena, criminalising destruction, conditioning charitable registration, tax exemption and land title) was assertion — "no government will enforce" — rather than analysis. A carried an execution cost: its first rebuttal was clipped over the word cap, losing its closing weighing sentence. That trims but does not erase a clear edge.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's demonstration that B's "no archives, no discharge" fund grants the church finality certified against a disclosure the church itself indexed — i.e. that B had rebuilt the Irish indemnity it called a betrayal — and B's inability in Rebuttal 2 or closing to explain how completeness could ever be certified.</best_rebuttal>
